name: High-assurance identity and access gates for sensitive crypto systems

attribution.legal_posture: A named Coinbase executive described attempted DPRK-linked applicants and the company's defensive adaptations in a public interview. The account covers applicant attempts and defensive response; it records no incident report, successful-hire finding, legal requirement, adjudication, case count, loss report, or sensitive-access finding.

caveats: The source describes attempted applicants and adaptations; successful Coinbase hiring of a DPRK worker and case count require separate case evidence.
Citizenship, family-location, and fingerprint requirements depend on jurisdiction and context; they provide no standalone proof of trustworthiness.

Nationality, citizenship, family location, ethnicity, appearance, accent, language, geography, compensation level, and one vendor or automated result require corroboration before any adverse or attribution decision.

The record retains bounded source context; wallet addresses, transaction identifiers, accounts, payment credentials, raw screening matches, people, personas, entities, victims, images, biometric material, identity documents, private data, and sensitive selectors stay outside it.
Publish the defensible abstraction: require lawful, high-assurance physical identity proofing and role-based access gates for unusually sensitive crypto systems.

Stablecoin use, multiple payment destinations, third-party payment requests, and low rates occur in legitimate global contracting; each requires lawful corroboration and documented human review before any inference.
The record is a source-qualified defensive control abstraction; person, entity, account, incident, and attribution profiles remain separate record types.

infrastructure.evidence_class: first-party executive statement about employer controls
infrastructure.description: Coinbase's chief executive described a response to repeated DPRK-linked remote applicants that separates ordinary recruitment from sensitive-system eligibility: live-camera checks, physical U.S. orientation, fingerprinting and compartmentalized access before sensitive work.
